title: Police not at fault in man's death, SIU determines
article: The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) ruled this week that there is no cause to criminally charge police after the post-arrest death of a Toronto man in connection with an incident in Etobicoke in November of 2006.

James Cornish, the director of the SIU, issued a statement Tuesday following the conclusion of the more than year-long investigation into the death of Jasen Drnasin - which involved three investigators, two forensic identification technicians, 16 witness officers and 16 civilian witnesses.

"Whatever the precise cause of Mr. Drnasin's unfortunate death, there are no reasonable grounds in my view to believe the death resulted from a criminal offence committed by any of the involved officers," he said, characterizing the incident as a "prolonged struggle with an individual exhibiting extraordinary strength."

According to the SIU's findings, Drnasin's altercation with both TTC Special Constables and Toronto Police Service (TPS) officers occurred in the area of Eglinton Avenue and Royal York Road on Nov. 12, 2006. Shortly after his arrest, he went into medical distress and was transported to hospital, where he remained in critical condition until his death on Nov. 27, 2006.

The SIU determined Drnasin boarded a southbound TTC bus on Islington Avenue late on the afternoon of Nov. 12, and without provocation, punched a stranger. The man got off the bus and called police, only to meet Drnasin again several hours later on an eastbound bus on Eglinton Avenue. The unnamed victim called police again.

Drnasin exited the bus at Islington Avenue and the man got off at Royal York Road. While the victim waited for police to arrive, yet another eastbound bus carrying Drnasin as a passenger stopped at Royal York. The TTC driver was informed of the situation and asked passengers to exit the bus onto another eastbound bus, which had pulled in behind him. Drnasin followed suit.

Two TTC Special Constables were first to arrive on the scene and attempted to arrest him - when he physically resisted, pepper foam was used in an attempt to control him. The constables were unable to subdue Drnasin and a TTC employee suffered a broken arm during the struggle, the SIU reported.

After breaking free, Drnasin fled the bus and ran from the scene, and Toronto police officers were called in. When police caught up with him, they ordered him to stop, but were ignored, the report said.

"The TPS officers delivered knee strikes and punches to Mr. Drnasin with the intent of gaining his compliance," Cornish said, noting there was no evidence that he was choked in any way. "The officers held Mr. Drnasin down and restrained his limbs. This was an entirely reasonable response to the situation facing the officers."

The struggle continued for about eight minutes, until more officers were brought in. Drnasin then went into medical distress, and was treated on the scene by Toronto Fire and EMS. As an oxygen mask was placed on Drnasin, he continued to struggle against his restraints. He died in hospital two weeks later.
"In my view, the force used cannot be characterized as excessive or unwarranted. Mr. Drnasin's death cannot be attributed to unreasonable force used by the police," Cornish said.

The SIU is a civilian government agency that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians, which have resulted in serious injury or death. Under Section 113 of the Police Services Act, the Director of the SIU has the authority to decide whether or not charges are warranted based on the findings of an investigation. The Director's decision is reported to the Attorney General.
